SMTO-EXE-0044 — The forced reset wasn't confirmed, so nothing was done

GUID: c96139b0-227a-4b4a-b454-197087863ba2
Slug: resource-reset-confirmation-required
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to end a blocking job by force, but the request didn't include your confirmation. The job was not ended and nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload this page so the task shows its current recovery card. An out-of-date page can send the reset without your confirmation.
  2. In the recovery card, read the warning about ending the blocking job. Changes that job already made are kept. Ending a job by force is a big step, so SMTO only does it when you clearly confirm it.
  3. If you still want to go ahead, select Resolve forcefully by terminating job. Otherwise select Wait until the job state changes. Either choice sends a complete request that SMTO can act on.

What success looks like

  • The card shows Blocking job claims restored, or says SMTO is waiting for the job state to change.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep sending the same reset request; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The resource-reconciliation route received a reset decision with reset_confirmed false and rejected it before terminating any job or resetting its claim.

What this means

  • The resource reset route received reset_confirmed false and rejected the destructive recovery decision before applying it. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The resource reset route received reset_confirmed false and rejected the destructive recovery decision before applying it.

How to diagnose it

  • Review the current reset scope, affected recorded owners and warning in the existing recovery controls.

How to fix it

  • Resubmit the reset to the run's resource-reconciliation endpoint (agent_runtime.api.agent_ui_support.route_groups.resource_reconciliation) with reset_confirmed: true only after reviewing the current reset_warning and blocker details. The Agent UI recovery card sets this flag itself, so an unconfirmed request usually means an outdated page or a direct API client.
  • Inspect the displayed reset scope and risks. Confirm it only if that exact reset is intended.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Explicit confirmation for the current supported reset is recorded before its owning control flow proceeds.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
